In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

1128381504993955822.desc: Leaders and representatives from 21 member economies of APEC gather in Shenzhen, China for the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting. 1128381504993955823.desc: Fernanda, an entrepreneur from Mexico, has launched a trade services platform in the Greater Bay Area to help Latin American companies enter the Chinese market. For her, APEC is not just a concept on paper-it is part of her everyday work, from business negotiations to cross-border partnerships. Her team also helps Chinese companies explore Latin American markets, creating new opportunities for shared growth across the Asia-Pacific.

1128381504993955824.desc:
From interactive smart bins to public installations that respond to emotions, Australian product designer and Sencity co-founder Steven Bai is exploring how AI can be integrated into streets, buildings and public spaces - taking technology beyond screens and into everyday life.
From conceiving his startup idea to putting down roots in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, he is drawing on China's well-developed manufacturing ecosystem to bring Physical AI innovations to global markets. #APECChina2026 #APECChinaYear

1128381504993955825.desc: For Dr. Mark Ceolin, Shanghai is more than a gateway to China and the Asia-Pacific - it is where his personal journey and China-Canada connections took root. Having witnessed the city’s remarkable rise since the 2000s, he has dedicated himself to helping Canadian companies grow in China. Seeing is believing. Today, Mark guides a growing number of Canadian businesses to experience a welcoming market full of emerging possibilities.

1128381504993955826.desc: What happens when a Filipino coffee lover turns his passion into a business in China? Meet Diel, founder of Nearby Coffee in Quanzhou, Fujian Province, who is serving up more than just a good brew! He's building cultural connections between China and the Philippines, with plans to take his business across borders. #APECChina2026 #APECChinaYear

1128381504993955827.desc:
China now produces two out of every three electric vehicles sold worldwide. How did this transformation of the global auto industry happen so fast, and what does it mean for once-dominant European carmakers? Is it an unfair advantage or simply smart strategising?
Jen Copestake presents Shocking the System: Why China is winning the EV race—a documentary that takes you inside China's EV revolution. 
We explore the supply chain dominance that's slashed production costs, and the 'Corner Overtaking' strategy that has helped Chinese automakers leapfrog their global competitors.

1128381504993955828.desc:
China's humanoid robot revolution is no longer science fiction. It is unfolding right now. From Shenzhen's first robot 6S store to advanced research labs in Shanghai, we meet the pioneers building machines that can walk, talk, fold laundry, stock supermarket shelves, and even box.

Featuring insights from Dr Liu Shaoshan, Unitree Robotics, and AgiBot, this episode explores embodied AI, robotic hands with human-like touch, and the race to bring humanoids into factories and eventually into our homes. The question is no longer if they will enter our world, but when.

1128381504993955829.desc: What makes Shenzhen such an attractive place to launch a business? With the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting approaching, all eyes are on this innovation-driven city in China. But beyond its reputation as a tech hub, what does it actually take to turn a big idea into a real product here? In this episode of #BizPodcast, CGTN talks with two entrepreneurs about why they chose Shenzhen, how they bring ideas to market, and what young founders should know before starting a business. Would you consider starting a business in Shenzhen? What would you want to know first?

1128381504993955830.desc: CGTN's new special program "Vive La Tech" focuses on some of the coolest science collaborations between China and France. In this episode, we shift our attention to climate change and the grape at risk. Follow our reporter Yang Zhao into the vineyards.

1128381504993955831.desc: In this episode of CGTN's special program "Vive La Tech," we dive into the "frozen world". In low-temperature metrology, scientists created the world's most precise temperature measuring device, from 5 to 24.5 kelvin, providing a source for all thermometers around the world. Join CGTN reporter Yang Zhao to explore how such an innovative partnership can open new doors for fundamental science.

1128381504993955832.desc:
Guangdong Province has long been one of China's pioneers in opening up. As the country's leading provincial trader, Guangdong is deepening economic ties with the Asia-Pacific through trade, innovation and closer cooperation. From coffee machines made in Shunde to robots developed through Guangdong-Hong Kong collaboration, companies are finding new opportunities across the region.
The province has been China's largest provincial trader for 40 years, with last year's imports and exports topping 9 trillion yuan (about 1.3 trillion US dollars) and more than 20 million market entities. Shunde is now the world's largest coffee machine production base, with Gemilai alone shipping to over 60 countries and selling more than two million units. Leveraging the Greater Bay Area's innovation hub, Guangdong is also advancing Guangdong-Hong Kong robotics projects and, as Shenzhen hosts APEC this year, aims to deepen regional industrial and supply-chain links for shared growth.

1128381504993955833.desc: As China hosts APEC 2026, regional integration is taking center stage. In southern China's Greater Bay Area, cities like Zhuhai, Hengqin, and Macao are operating like a single supply chain network, linking automated factories with global talent and capital. To see how this cross-border teamwork helps brands go global, CGTN's Yu Hongyu takes us inside a hair dryer factory in Zhuhai.
